lesson_title: Finance and Data Essentials: The Paper 1 Revision Run
hook_text: One flu-week mark dragged her average down 8 points. The median never flinched.
clip_script: Five marks on the fridge door: 62, 58, 71, 65 — and one disaster, 24, from the week she had flu. Her uncle adds them up: 280 divided by 5 — she's a 56 learner, he says. But arrange the marks first: 24, 58, 62, 65, 71. The middle one — the median — is 62. So who's telling the truth? Take the flu mark away and the mean of the rest jumps to 64. ONE bad mark dragged the mean down eight points, while the median never moved — because the median only cares about position, not how bad the bad mark was. That's a full exam answer: name the outlier, say which way it pulls. Now the till: a slip says R287,50, VAT included. To find the price before tax, DIVIDE by 1,15 — back to R250 exactly. Never take 15 percent off the total; the tax was charged on the smaller number. And the tuck shop: chips bought at R6,50, sold at R10. Mark-up isn't 35 percent — it's 3,50 over 6,50, nearly 54 percent, measured against what SHE paid. Paper 1 is 90 marks of finance and 53 of data — and these are exactly the moves it pays for.
visual_style: A report card pinned on a fridge with magnets, marks rearranging themselves into order; a red outlier mark dragging a see-saw labelled MEAN while a steady pin labelled MEDIAN holds still; a till slip splitting into 250 and 37,50; chips packets stacking into a percentage bar.
mood: Family-kitchen real talk, sharp and reassuring.
pacing: Quick fridge-door setup, a beat on the 56-versus-62 argument, brisk VAT and mark-up finishes with numbers landing like till beeps.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and walk into Paper 1 knowing exactly where its 150 marks live.
